2026-11-21 / Project Confluence / Development note

Project Confluence — Corner Modules and Adjustable Building Dimensions

Adding instanced corner modules to the four-sided building shell and testing how they respond to changes in facade dimensions and floor count.

Add corner modules to the building shell

The previous building prototype positioned four modular facades around a rectangular footprint. I extended the shell with four corner modules using an Instanced Static Mesh component. These pieces sit at the junctions between the facades, giving each corner a consistent element that can be placed as part of the building assembly.

The current corner mesh is used to test the structural arrangement in the environment. Its final appearance can be developed alongside the rest of the residential building.

Test changes to the building dimensions

I tested the shell by changing its width, depth, and floor count. The facades and corner instances updated as the dimensions changed, and the corner height scaled with the number of floors. This allowed the same assembly to accommodate different building proportions while keeping the corners aligned with the surrounding walls.

The comparison shows Facade B with two and three columns at a module width of 200 cm and a height of two floors. The facade extends further in the second configuration, while the corner remains positioned at the edge of the building.

Organize the building workflow

After testing the corner placement, I organized the building logic under BuildBuildingShell. The workflow calculates the dimensions used by the shell, builds the corner instances, and positions the facades. Separating these steps makes the current assembly easier to inspect as the building system develops.

The next step is to add a simple roof slab that responds to the footprint. With the basic shell in place, I can then return to the architectural and visual development of the residential building.
